edges.prerequisite: Forwarding vs. Routing in the Network Layer
edges.rationale: Input/output port processing is the hardware realization of the per-router forwarding function, so the forwarding-vs-routing distinction must come first.

edges.prerequisite: Forwarding vs. Routing in the Network Layer
edges.rationale: The switching fabric and queues are the internal mechanisms that accomplish forwarding within a router, which only makes sense once forwarding is defined.

edges.prerequisite: Forwarding vs. Routing in the Network Layer
edges.rationale: Traditional IP forwarding details destination-based forwarding using the forwarding table, a concept introduced by the forwarding-vs-routing overview.

edges.prerequisite: Forwarding vs. Routing in the Network Layer
edges.rationale: Generalized forwarding extends the forwarding function beyond destination-based lookup, requiring the basic forwarding concept first.

edges.prerequisite: Forwarding vs. Routing in the Network Layer
edges.rationale: SDN explicitly separates the data plane from the control plane, which is precisely the forwarding/routing distinction, so that distinction is a direct prerequisite.
The switching fabric moves packets from input ports to output ports and queues form at those ports, so port operation must be understood first.
Generalized forwarding is defined in contrast to destination-based forwarding ('rather than the destination address alone'), so traditional forwarding must be learned first.
SDN controllers compute and distribute match+action flow tables, which are an instance of generalized forwarding, so generalized forwarding is a prerequisite.
